samples.summary: The per-branch round directory is keyed on `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`, which is the literal string `HEAD` in a detached HEAD — so every detached checkout shares one round counter and one carry-forward store.
samples.evidence: `cmdReview` (line 808) reads `branch = git(["rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD"])` and feeds it to `reviewBase(branch)` (line 723-727), which hashes that string into `<tmp>/wafflebase-self-review/<safe>-<hash>`. In a detached HEAD — mid-rebase, `git bisect`, and notably the default `actions/checkout` state in CI (the docs added in this diff say CI is one of the two supported modes: "CI pins `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from repository secrets") — `--abbrev-ref HEAD` returns the string `HEAD`, not a branch name. Every such run therefore resolves to the same base directory. On any machine or self-hosted runner where that temp path persists between runs, `priorFindingsFor` (line 778) reads `round-N/<lens>/verdict.json` written while reviewing a *different* change and writes those findings into this round's `--prior-findings`, i.e. another branch's findings are re-raised as blockers here and fed into the verifier prompt; `nextRound` likewise inherits the other change's round count and can trip the 3-round bound (line 887) on a first round. `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` has no `--symbolic-full-name`/`@{u}` fallback and there is no detached-HEAD guard anywhere in `cmdReview`.

samples.summary: `mkdirSync(base, …)` is the one unguarded filesystem call on the review path: a base that exists as a file, or an unwritable parent, throws an uncaught exception past every `fail()` refusal around it.
samples.evidence: Line 836 `mkdirSync(base, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });` has no try/catch, while the immediately following leaf and ancestor inspections (840-862) are carefully wrapped and route to `fail(...)`. `mkdirSync` with `recursive: true` still throws `EEXIST`/`ENOTDIR` when the path exists as a regular file or symlink-to-file, and `EACCES` when the parent is not writable — both easy to hit via `--out` (e.g. `--out /tmp/notes.txt`). The result is a raw Node stack trace instead of the `refusing to use the review directory …` message the guard right below was written to produce, and it happens *before* `unsafeBaseReason` ever gets to say `it is not a directory` (522) — a branch that is therefore unreachable for the pre-existing-file case it names.

samples.summary: `roundBoundNotice`'s docblock states the bound is "Deliberately NOT a refusal", but the call site refuses unless `--force` — the comment documents the opposite of the implemented behaviour.
samples.evidence: Lines 219-223: "Deliberately NOT a refusal. … a hard stop would also block the legitimate case … So it says the thing a refusal would be trying to say, and lets the human decide." The call site at 886-888 does exactly what that paragraph says it does not: `const notice = roundBoundNotice(round); if (notice && !args.force) return fail(notice);`. The block comment at 880-885 ('REFUSED, not warned') contradicts the function's own docblock a few hundred lines above. A maintainer reading the helper will conclude round 4 runs with a warning; it exits 1. (The same helper's returned text does name `--force`, so only the docblock is stale.)

samples.summary: `roundsOnDisk` can throw `ENOTDIR`, which breaks `priorFindingsFor`'s documented "Never throws" contract and crashes the command outside every catch.
samples.evidence: `roundsOnDisk` (754-769) takes the names `roundsIn` matched and calls `readdirSync(path.join(base, `round-${round}`), { withFileTypes: true })` (757) with no try/catch; the inner try only wraps the `verdict.json` read. If an entry literally named `round-2` is a regular file — reachable when the caller aims `--out` at a directory they also use for something else, which the `--fresh` bounding comment at 701-712 explicitly anticipates — `readdirSync` throws `ENOTDIR`. `priorFindingsFor` (778-788) calls it on line 779 *outside* its per-lens try, despite the docblock at 774 saying "Never throws", and `cmdReview` calls it unguarded at line 878, so the failure surfaces as an uncaught stack trace rather than the fail-quiet 'carry fewer findings' direction the rest of this path is built on.

samples.summary: `process.exit(1)` fires immediately after writing the multi-line blocking-findings report to stderr, which truncates that report when stderr is a pipe.
samples.evidence: Lines 986-994 write the lens list, then `renderBlockingFindings(...)` (unbounded in line count — one entry per blocking finding across every failing lens, each finding three lines), then the follow-up instructions, and then call `process.exit(1)`. Node's stdout/stderr are asynchronous when they are a pipe rather than a TTY, and `process.exit` does not flush pending writes — so exactly the surface this change exists to add (the developer-readable findings the old code never printed) is the part at risk of being cut off whenever the command is run under a harness, `| tee`, or `2>&1 | less`. `process.exitCode = 1` followed by a normal return has the same semantics without the truncation.

samples.summary: `--out ""` silently falls back to the per-branch default instead of being a usage error, unlike every other malformed value `reviewArgsError` catches.
samples.evidence: `reviewArgsError` (587-597) rejects `--out` only when it is not a string, so `--out ""` passes validation; line 814 then does `args.out ? path.resolve(args.out) : reviewBase(branch)` and the empty string is falsy, so the run quietly uses the default temp base while the caller believes they redirected it. The function's own docblock frames exactly this class of thing ('silent data loss rather than a usage error') as what it exists to prevent.

samples.summary: The first "a forged `infra` key cannot suppress a finding" test asserts `[]` and attributes it to the forged `infra` key, but the fixture is dropped by the `lane: "backlog"` filter — and its sibling test asserts the opposite outcome for the same claim.
samples.evidence: The fixture is `{ severity: "critical", file: "a.ts", summary: "…", infra: true, lane: "backlog", valid: false }` and the comment says "It is dropped as an infra record only because of the forged key...". `carryForwardFindings` applies `.filter((f) => f.lane !== "backlog")` (prior-findings.mjs:159) before the projection, so the record never reaches `isInfraRecord` at all — it is dropped by the lane filter regardless of the `infra` key, and the assertion would still pass if the infra handling were deleted entirely. The very next test ("…cannot suppress a real finding") asserts that a forged `infra: true` finding IS carried, which is the actual behaviour; the two tests read as contradicting each other about the same property.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described: cmdReview reads the branch via `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` (spec-to-pr.mjs:806-811) with no detached-HEAD handling or fallback, and feeds that raw string to reviewBase (723-727), which sanitizes/hashes it into <tmpdir>/wafflebase-self-review/<safe>-<hash>; that path is the default base whenever --out is absent (814). In any detached HEAD the string is literally "HEAD", so all detached runs share one base, and the persisted contents drive priorFindingsFor (778-788) into --prior-findings (878, 898) and nextRound/roundBoundNotice (879, 886-887) — i.e. another change's findings re-raised as blockers and an inherited round count that can refuse a first round. No guard exists: reviewArgsError (587-597) validates only arg shapes, the CLI dispatch (1001-1004) adds nothing, and grep finds no `symbolic-ref`/detached check in the file. The reviewer's CI justification is partly wrong — CI runs review-panel.mjs directly (.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:882, agent-review-on-demand.yml:382), and the "CI pins a pooled credential" wording is only ambientAuthNotice's comment (239-268) — but that only trims the blast radius; the local detached states it also names (rebase, bisect, checkout of a sha/tag) are reachable and the tmpdir base persists between runs. Broken state-keying invariant with cross-run contamination is squarely in the correctness lane, so neither not-present, already-guarded, nor out-of-scope applies.
